Oman competed at the 2016 Summer Olympics in [[Rio de Janeiro]], Brazil, when the event was held from 5 to 21 August 2016. This was the nation's ninth consecutive appearance at the Summer Olympics. Four Omani athletes, two men and two women, were selected to compete in athletics and shooting at the Games. Among them were sprinter [[Barakat Al-Harthi]], the lone returning Olympian from the previous Games.

During their debuts, [[Mazoon Al-Alawi]] competed in running while [[Wadha Al-Balushi]] was the first woman to represent Oman in shooting. Rifle shooter [[Hamed Said Al-Khatri]] was the nation's [[flag bearer]] in the [[2016 Summer Olympics opening ceremony|opening ceremony]]. None of the runners progressed past the heats and the shooters did not advance beyond the qualification rounds. Overall, both Al-Harthi and Al-Balushi had the highest placing for Oman with their 26th-place finishes in the [[Athletics at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's 100 metres|men's 100 metres]] and [[Shooting at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Women's 10 metre air pistol|women's 10 m air pistol]] events.

==Background==
In 1982, the [[Oman Olympic Committee]] was created and became part of the [[International Olympic Committee]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Grasso |first1=John |last2=Mallon |first2=Bill |last3=Heijmans |first3=Jeoren |title=Historical Dictionary of the Olympic Movement |date=2015 |publisher=Rowman & Littlefield |location=Lanham and London |isbn=9781442248595 |page=453 |edition=Fifth |chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=uCN1CQAAQBAJ&pg=PA453 |access-date=11 May 2021 |chapter=Oman (OMA)}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=History |url=https://ooc.om/?page_id=2255&lang=en&csrt=15306514003882045916 |website=Oman Olympic Committee |access-date=11 May 2021}}</ref> After appearing at the [[1984 Summer Olympics]], Oman competed in seven consecutive Summer Olympics leading up to the [[2016 Summer Olympics]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Oman (OMA) |url=https://www.olympedia.org/countries/OMA |website=Olympedia |access-date=11 May 2021}}</ref> As part of his Olympic training, [[Barakat Al-Harthi]] ran in several countries including [[Bahrain]] and [[Bulgaria]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Oman's only man: Single sprinter to compete in Rio Olympics |url=https://www.albawaba.com/editorchoice/oman%E2%80%99s-only-man-single-sprinter-compete-rio-olympics-832206 |access-date=26 May 2021 |work=Al Bawaba |date=23 April 2016}}</ref><ref name=Albawabajune2016>{{cite news |title=Oman's Barakat al Harthi shatters 100m national record again |url=https://www.albawaba.com/sport/omans-barakat-al-harthi-shatters-100m-national-record-again-850952 |access-date=26 May 2021 |work=Al Bawaba |date=12 June 2016}}</ref> While flying to Rio to compete at the 2016 Summer Olympics, Al-Harthi missed his [[layover]] and lost some of his [[sports equipment]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Barakat Al Harthy: An Omani competing at the 2016 Rio Olympics |url=https://timesofoman.com/article/19320-barakat-al-harthy-an-omani-competing-at-the-2016-rio-olympics |agency=Times News Service |access-date=29 May 2021 |work=Times of Oman |date=12 October 2016}}</ref>

In the 2016 Olympics held from 5 to 21 August, Al-Harthi was competing in his second Olympics after appearing at the [[2012 Summer Olympics]],<ref>{{cite web |title=2016 Summer Olympics |url=https://www.olympedia.org/editions/59 |website=Olympedia |access-date=30 May 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Barakat Al-Harthi |url=https://www.olympedia.org/athletes/125145 |website=Olympedia |access-date=11 May 2021}}</ref> while runner [[Mazoon Al-Alawi]] was making her Olympic debut.<ref>{{cite web |title=Marzoon Al-Alawi |url=https://www.olympedia.org/athletes/131333 |website=Olympedia |access-date=12 May 2021}}</ref> The other Olympians making their first appearances for Oman were shooters [[Hamed Said Al-Khatri]] and [[Wadha Al-Balushi]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Hamed Said Al-Khatri |url=https://www.olympedia.org/athletes/135419 |website=Olympedia |access-date=12 May 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Wadha Al-Balushi |url=https://www.olympedia.org/athletes/131334 |website=Olympedia |access-date=12 May 2021}}</ref> Al-Khatri was selected as the first woman to represent Oman in shooting.<ref>{{cite news |title=Ready, Aim, Run |url=https://issuu.com/eshabiba/docs/t04-08-2016/39 |access-date=27 May 2021 |work=Times of Oman |date=4 August 2016 |at=The Road to Rio p.3 |via=Issuu}}</ref> Al-Khatri was the [[flag bearer]] at the [[2016 Summer Olympics opening ceremony|opening ceremony]] and a volunteer carried the flag at the [[2016 Summer Olympics closing ceremony|closing ceremony]].<ref name=TimesofOmanAugust2016/><ref>{{cite web |title=Rio 2016 Closing Ceremony - Flag Bearers |url=https://stillmed.olympic.org/media/Document%20Library/OlympicOrg/News/2016/08/2016-08-21-Rio-2016-Closing-Ceremony-Flag-Bearers.pdf |website=International Olympic Committee |access-date=12 May 2021 |page=2 |date=21 August 2016}}</ref> Apart from the four Omani competitors, the country sent several coaches and sports executives to the 2016 Olympics.<ref name=TimesofOmanAugust2016>{{cite news |title=Shooter Wadha launches Oman's campaign at Rio Olympics |url=https://timesofoman.com/article/14751-shooter-wadha-launches-omans-campaign-at-rio-olympics |access-date=11 May 2021 |work=Times of Oman |agency=Times News Service |date=6 August 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Oman at the 2016 Summer Olympics |url=https://www.olympedia.org/countries/OMA/editions/59 |website=Olympedia |access-date=12 May 2021}}</ref>

==Athletics (track & field)==
{{main article|Athletics at the 2016 Summer Olympics|Athletics at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Qualification}} 
Al-Harthi qualified for the Olympics with a time of 10.16 seconds at the [[2015 Military World Games]].<ref name=Albawabajune2016/> In 2016, his Olympic qualifying time of 10.05 seconds was 0.11 seconds faster than the required time to enter the [[Athletics at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's 100 metres|men's 100 metres]].<ref>{{cite web |title=World Ranking List for Olympic Games Qualification Track & field events - Men |url=http://www.iaaf.org/download/downloadresultinfo?filename=2c8232f9-37a4-4277-813c-2077b1eb05b2.pdf&urlSlug=rio-2016-iaaf-world-ranking-lists-mens-trac |website=IAAF |access-date=26 May 2021 |page=3}}</ref><ref name=insidethegames>{{cite web|title=IAAF Games of the XXX Olympiad – Rio 2016 Entry Standards|url=http://www.insidethegames.biz/media/file/559/IAAF%20Rio%202016%20standards.pdf|website=IAAF|access-date=18 April 2015}}</ref> On 13 August, Al-Harthi did not appear in the preliminary round and competed in the sixth race of the heats.<ref>{{cite web |title=100 Metres men &#124; The XXXI Olympic Games |url=https://www.worldathletics.org/results/olympic-games/2016/the-xxxi-olympic-games-7093747/men/100-metres/heats/result |website=World Athletics |at=Heats Result |access-date=27 May 2021}}</ref> Al-Harthi finished in third in his heat with a time of 10.22 seconds.<ref>{{cite news |title=Athletics: Men's 100m |url=http://www.bbc.com/sport/olympics/rio-2016/results/sports/athletics/mens-100m |access-date=27 May 2021 |work=BBC |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170405134706/http://www.bbc.com/sport/olympics/rio-2016/results/sports/athletics/mens-100m |archive-date=5 April 2017}}</ref> His placing meant Al-Harthi did not qualify as one of the first two runners in his individual heat. As he also did not have one of the eight fastest times from the remaining runners, Al-Harthi did not progress to the semi-finals.<ref name=olympediamens100m>{{cite web |title=2016 Summer Olympics / Athletics / 100 metres, Men |url=https://www.olympedia.org/results/358560 |website=Olympedia |access-date=27 May 2021}}</ref> Out of 84 competitors, Al-Harthi finished in a tie for 26th place overall.<ref>{{cite web |title=2016 Summer Olympics Results |url=https://www.espn.com/olympics/summer/2016/results/_/discipline/3/event/256 |website=ESPN |access-date=27 May 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160815013608/https://www.espn.com/olympics/summer/2016/results/_/discipline/3/event/256 |archive-date=15 August 2016 |at=Men's 100M}}</ref>

Mazoon Al-Alawi entered the 2016 Olympics as a [[Wild card (sports)|wild card]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Oman delegation gear up for Rio Olympics |url=http://timesofoman.com/article/88904/Sports/Oman/Oman-delegation-gear-up-for-Rio-Olympics|work=Times of Oman|publisher=Times News Agency|date=27 July 2016|access-date=29 May 2021}}</ref> Her entry time of 12.04 seconds was 0.72 seconds slower than the Olympic qualifying time for the [[Athletics at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Women's 100 metres|women's 100 metres]].<ref name=insidethegames/><ref>{{cite web |title=100 Metres women &#124; The XXXI Olympic Games |url=https://www.worldathletics.org/competitions/olympic-games/the-xxxi-olympic-games-7093747/results/women/100-metres/preliminary-round/startlist |website=World Athletics |at=Preliminary Round Startlist |access-date=27 May 2021}}</ref> On 12 August, Al-Alawi finished third in the second heat of the preliminary round with a time of 12.30 seconds, which qualified her as one of the two fastest remaining runners following the top two finishers of all of the heats.<ref>{{cite web |title=100 Metres women &#124; The XXXI Olympic Games |url=https://www.worldathletics.org/competitions/olympic-games/the-xxxi-olympic-games-7093747/results/women/100-metres/preliminary-round/result |website=World Athletics |at=Preliminary Round Result |access-date=27 May 2021}}</ref> In the subsequent round (held the same day) Al-Alawi came in eighth in the seventh heat.<ref name=olympediawomens100m>{{cite web |title=2016 Summer Olympics / Athletics / 100 metres, Women |url=https://www.olympedia.org/results/358986 |website=Olympedia |access-date=27 May 2021}}</ref> She did not automatically advance to the next round as she did not finish in the top two of her heat and, with a time of 12.43 seconds, she was slower than the next eight qualifiers and so she did not progress past the heats.<ref>{{cite web |title=100 Metres women &#124; The XXXI Olympic Games |url=https://www.worldathletics.org/competitions/olympic-games/the-xxxi-olympic-games-7093747/results/women/100-metres/heats/result |website=World Athletics |at=Heats Result |access-date=27 May 2021}}</ref> Al-Alawi finished 62nd overall out of 80 runners.<ref>{{cite web |title=2016 Summer Olympics |url=http://www.espn.com/olympics/summer/2016/results/_/event/302/discipline/3 |website=ESPN |access-date=27 May 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160817141442/http://www.espn.com/olympics/summer/2016/results/_/event/302/discipline/3 |at=Athletics Women's 100m |archive-date=17 August 2016}}</ref>

==Shooting==
{{main article|Shooting at the 2016 Summer Olympics|Shooting at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Qualification}}

Before the Olympics, each shooter required a [[Olympic quota allocation system|Quota Place]] and Minimum Qualification Score.<ref>{{cite web |title=Olympic Games Qualification |url=http://www.issf-sports.org/competitions/ogqualification.ashx |website=International Shooting Sport Federation |access-date=10 May 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160820164620/http://www.issf-sports.org/competitions/ogqualification.ashx |archive-date=20 August 2016}}</ref> With invitations from the Tripartite Commission, Quota Places were given to [[Hamed Said Al-Khatri]] and [[Wadha Al-Balushi]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Dea |first=Marco Dalla |title=Rio 2016 Quota Places: the distribution rules |url=https://www.issf-sports.org/news.ashx?newsid=2002 |website=International Shooting Sports Federation |access-date=10 May 2021 |date=2 February 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Rio 2016: Shooting sport Quota Places overview after exchanges and re-allocations |last=Dea |first=Marco Dalla |url=https://www.issf-sports.org/news.ashx?newsid=2583 |website=International Shooting Sport Federation |access-date=10 May 2021 |date=20 June 2016}}</ref> To qualify for the [[Shooting at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's 50 metre rifle three positions|men's 50 metre rifle three positions]] event, shooters needed at least 1135 points.<ref name=ISSFqualification>{{cite web |title=Minimum Qualification Score (MQS) |url=http://www.issf-sports.org/competitions/ogqualification/mqs_qualifiers.ashx |website=International Shooting Sport Federation |access-date=10 May 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160822083247/http://www.issf-sports.org/competitions/ogqualification/mqs_qualifiers.ashx |archive-date=22 August 2016}}</ref> Al-Khatri reached his requirement by scoring 1149 points at the [[2014 ISSF World Shooting Championships]] in this division.<ref>{{cite web |title=List of MQS Qualifiers per Olympic Event|url=http://www.issf-sports.org/competitions/ogqualification/mqs_qualifiers/list_of_mqs_qualifiers_per_olympic_event.ashx?event=FR3X40&evlinkid=100 |website=International Shooting Sport Federation |date=24 March 2016 |at=50m Rifle 3 Positions Men |access-date=10 May 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160826113622/http://www.issf-sports.org/competitions/ogqualification/mqs_qualifiers/list_of_mqs_qualifiers_per_olympic_event.ashx?event=FR3X40&evlinkid=100 |archive-date=26 August 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Hamed Said Alkhatri |url=https://www.issf-sports.org/athletes/athlete.ashx?personissfid=SHOMAM2405198501 |website=International Shooting Sport Federation |access-date=10 May 2021}}</ref> For the [[Shooting at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Women's 10 metre air pistol|women's 10 metre air pistol]] Olympic event, qualifiers needed 365 points or more.<ref name=ISSFqualification/> During the [[2015 ISSF World Cup]], Al-Balushi accumulated 381 points and reached her score requirement.<ref>{{cite web |title=Wadha Al Balushi |url=https://www.issf-sports.org/athletes/athlete.ashx?personissfid=SHOMAW3011198901 |website=International Shooting Sport Federation |access-date=11 May 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=List of MQS Qualifiers per Olympic Event |url=http://www.issf-sports.org/competitions/ogqualification/mqs_qualifiers/list_of_mqs_qualifiers_per_olympic_event.ashx?event=AP40&evlinkid=204 |website=International Shooting Sport Federation |access-date=11 May 2021 |archive-date=26 August 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160826113602/http://www.issf-sports.org/competitions/ogqualification/mqs_qualifiers/list_of_mqs_qualifiers_per_olympic_event.ashx?event=AP40&evlinkid=204 |date=24 March 2016 |at=10m Air Pistol Women}}</ref>

At his qualification round on 14 August, Al-Khatri scored 1138 points during the 50&nbsp;m rifle three positions event.<ref>{{cite news |title=Medals and results |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/ng-interactive/2016/aug/05/rio-olympics-2016-medal-table-and-results-in-full |at=Shooting Day 9 - Sun 14 50m Rifle 3 Positions Men's Qualification |access-date=24 May 2021 |work=The Guardian |date=5 August 2016}}</ref> While achieving 397 points in the [[prone position]] round for his highest score, Al-Khatri scored 40 ten-pointers during the three rounds, but his score was too low to make him one of the eight qualifiers for the final.<ref name=olympediathreepositions>{{cite web |title=2016 Summer Olympics / Shooting / Small-Bore Rifle, Three Positions, 50 metres, Men |url=https://www.olympedia.org/results/395714 |website=Olympedia |access-date=24 May 2021}}</ref> Out of 44 competitors, Al-Khatri finished overall in 43rd.<ref>{{cite web |title=Rio 2016 Shooting 50m rifle 3 positions (3x40 shots) men Results |url=https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/rio-2016/results/shooting/50m-rifle-3-positions-3x40-shots-men |website=International Olympic Committee |access-date=24 May 2021}}</ref>

On 7 August, Al-Balushi scored 379 points during qualification at the 10&nbsp;m air pistol Olympic competition.<ref>{{cite news |title=Olympics-Shooting-Women's 10m air pistol qualification results |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/olympics-shooting-women-results-idCNISS700484 |access-date=24 May 2021 |work=Reuters |date=7 August 2016}}</ref> While scoring five ten-pointers throughout the four rounds, Al-Balushi's highest score was 96 points in the third round. As she did not have one of the eight highest overall scores, Al-Balushi did not qualify for the final.<ref name=olympediaairpistol>{{cite web |title=2016 Summer Olympics / Shooting / Air Pistol, 10 metres, Women |url=https://www.olympedia.org/results/395743 |website=Olympedia |access-date=24 May 2021}}</ref> Overall, Al-Balushi finished 26th out of 44 competitors.<ref>{{cite web |title=Rio 2016 Shooting 10m Air Pistol women Results |url=https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/rio-2016/results/shooting/10m-air-pistol-women |website=International Olympic Committee |access-date=24 May 2021}}</ref>
